tip: Comparatives usually add -are: dyr becomes dyrare (more expensive). No separate word for more is needed.
Ses is an s-verb meaning see each other. Vi ses is the everyday way to say see you later.
Use åker for going by vehicle. Gå means to walk, so jag åker till jobbet means you ride or drive there.
Street names take på, not i: Vi bor på Vasagatan. The same på marks open surfaces.
Över means across when there is motion: går över gatan is to cross the street.
Strong verbs form the supine in -it: äta becomes ätit. Har ätit is the present perfect, has eaten.
Gå på bio is fixed: cinema takes på, not till. Same pattern in gå på restaurang and gå på museum.
Vid means by or beside, right next to something: bor vid havet is to live by the sea.
Innanför means inside a boundary, opposite of utanför (outside). Innanför grinden is inside the gate.
Cars take i, not på: sitta i bilen. Swedish treats the car as an enclosed space you sit inside.
Swedish picks a body-position verb: things lying flat use ligger, so katten ligger under bordet, not är.
Åt marks doing something for or on behalf of someone: han gör det åt mig means he does it for me.
Islands take på: bor på en ö. Swedish uses på, not i, for being on an island.
A definite noun with a demonstrative is marked twice: den boken (that book), both den and the ending -en.
Samma never takes an article or ending: samma kontor, samma dag. It stays unchanged in every gender and number.
Han becomes honom as an object: gett honom (gave him). Use honom after a verb or a preposition.
Klart after a verb marks completion: läst klart means finished reading, like äta klart, to finish eating.
Ha rätt, literally have right, is the idiom for being correct: du har rätt means you are right.
Equality uses lika plus adjective plus som: lika lång som means as tall as.
Om means whether after verbs like veta: vi vet inte om means we don't know whether.
After ett, adjectives add -t: ny becomes nytt in ett nytt jobb. Neuter nouns trigger this ending.
Man is the generic you or one: mer än man tror means more than you would think. It is not the word for man.
For a span of time use i: i femton år means for fifteen years. Swedish uses i where English uses for.
Så att means so that, marking purpose: sparar pengar så att vi kan köpa hus, save so we can buy a house.
Front something other than the subject and the verb still comes second: Varje sommar åker vi, verb before vi.
På grund av is the fixed phrase for because of: på grund av trafiken means because of the traffic.
Superlatives usually add -ast, but stor is irregular: störst (biggest). Stockholm är störst.
Comparisons use än for than: större än Danmark means bigger than Denmark. Än always follows the comparative.
